CommitId.description: A Git object id in full, lowercase hexadecimal form.

Epistemic.description:
How the event is known. V1 has two tiers and no more: Nodal watched it happen, or
somebody said so.

oneOf.description: Captured by Nodal from a shim, a hook or the Git state.
Declared by a person or an agent.

Objective.description: What the unit is for, in one line, as the person or agent stated it.

ProjectId.description: Identifies a project: one Git repository Nodal manages units for.

Slug.description: The CLI handle for a unit, derived from its branch.

Timestamp.description: A UTC instant, serialised as an RFC 3339 string.

UnitId.description: Identifies a `WorkUnit`. Stable for the life of the work, across machines.

UnitStatus.description:
Where a unit is in its life. The branch, not the directory, is the identity a
reviewer or another tool sees, so a unit outlives any one materialisation.

oneOf.description: Being worked on; holds its branch against other units.
Merged; runtime may be stopped, the delta is still kept.
Kept for the record only; nothing of it is running.

base_commit.description:
The commit the unit forked from, when it was recorded.

Written once, by the create, and never updated: a unit forks once. It is the
commit the person's own checkout was at, or the one `--from` named.

`None` means not recorded, which is every unit made before the column existed.
It never means a unit forked from nothing. A reader that needs a fork point and
finds `None` falls back to the merge base it used before, and says which of the
two it is reporting.

branch.description: The branch this unit owns. Unique among open units, enforced by the registry.

id.description: Identity of the unit; stable across machines and re-materialisations.

objective.description: The intent, when there is one. Adoption may recover it later.

objective_epistemic.description:
How the objective is known, when there is one: `stated` when a person or an
agent said what the unit is for, `observed` when adoption recovered it from the
records of the session that made the checkout. A recovered line is a reading of
somebody's opening prompt, not a statement of intent, and a person deciding what
to do with a unit three weeks later needs to be told which of the two they are
reading.

parent_branch.description: The branch the work started from, when it is known.

project_id.description: The project the unit belongs to.

status.description: Where the unit is in its life.

updated_at.description: When any of the above last changed.
